column1: # RECIPE_MEMORY.tsv - append-only lesson memory of recipe durable-extent-store-20261107 (RELOCATE_DURABLE_EXTENT_STORE): one row per lesson, appended in the same commit as the correction.

column4: the scout row named 'zero-copy mapped slices' and 'fs-pmem rows 2-5 should land first': the slices are the synexia-mllm oracle's API (the donor copies out of a READ_ONLY mapping), and rows 2-5 are all on master; check both claims against the donor bytes and master before scoping

the donor's read facade (synexia-storage-sdk StorageStore) has the same shape as the PMem region core but not its contract (length > 0, span <= size instead of size == length, positional FILE backend): restate the donor default (AUTO -> MAPPED_FILE) on java.nio inside the owner and HOLD the facade, instead of porting a second mapping SDK or binding a misfit

derived from delta-generator-20261106/relocate.py v3 by an exact-anchor script (18 anchors): DROP_BLOCK rows (a run of consecutive donor lines removed exactly once: an overload or a validation block naming a HELD type), HELD rows (relocate.py refuses any relocated file that still names a held type) and the drop_blocks provenance column; first run changed=5, every later run changed=0

jdk_naming's SEGMENT_DOT rule renames schema ids (synexia.content-extent.v1 -> m3.content-extent.v1), which changes every identity hash; the recipe must emit the renamed ids itself (SCHEMA_ID SUBST rows) so jdk_naming apply stays a no-op and relocate.py --check stays changed=0, and the differential must compare against the donor with exactly those rows applied (the raw donor still matches on every non-identity line)
column5: jdk_naming plan moves=0 rewrites=0 refusals=0; dump donor-m3/relocated IDENTICAL

column4: a READ_ONLY MappedByteBuffer keeps the blob file locked until it is collected: the donor's own ExtentStandaloneProof fails on Windows when it truncates a blob it read ('user-mapped section open'), identically on the relocated store; the dump therefore tampers only blobs its JVM never mapped, and the proof runs in differential.sh, not in verify.py's host and image lanes
column5: differential.sh lane c: proof donor/relocated IDENTICAL (both stop at the truncation)

column4: verify.py keeps a closed inventory of src/test/java (any new test source raises 'module contract inventory changed'): new JUnit classes join maven_junit_sources through apply.py; a main that must not run on the host and image lanes stays in the recipe directory
column5: apply.py EDITS.tsv; python verify.py manual run reaches the same pre-existing M3FileDeltaSelfTest failure on Windows before and after

column4: a pass-through FileSystemProvider over the default provider counts every provider and FileChannel step of one store call (plus a torn half-write per write) and Runtime.halt()s a child JVM before the chosen step; it reaches every step the store takes, including temp-file creation inside Files.createTempFile and the directory open of syncDirectory; the PassThroughFileSystem of the OpenJDK tests lacks newFileChannel and is GPL-2.0-only
the sparse worktree has no .gitignore for m3/file/target: 'git add m3/file' staged 270 build outputs; stage explicit paths only

bash reads a script while it runs: editing differential.sh during a run shifted the text under the interpreter (a syntax error at the last lines and a stale javap expectation); never edit a running gate script, rerun it whole
column5: diff1.log line 157 syntax error; rerun in verify.sh

column4: jdk_naming's KEBAB rule rewrites a private repository name inside Java comments (the mllm repository became m3-mllm): name such repositories only in the .tsv/.md lineage files, which the naming recipe never rewrites
column5: jdk_naming apply KEBAB=1, then plan 0/0/0 after the javadoc names ORACLE_CLASSIFICATION.tsv
